$comment: UCDA-000001 CONSTITUTIONAL DECISION REGISTER — DATA ONLY. AUTHORITY = NONE (DERIVED TRUTH).
This file is the single extensible declaration consumed by ucda_engine.py. It is the
machine-readable DISPOSITION OVERLAY mandated by CEP-002 Article 28 over the decision
registers that already exist. Adding a decision, a lifecycle stage, a disposition or a
work package is an entry here and requires NO change to the engine.
* NOT a decision register in its own right. Every entry carries a source_register
that is the LOCATED authoritative register of that decision (CEP-002 Art 28.3).
No decision originates here. Zero Parallel Authority.
* NOT a registry. It allocates no identity. The sole registration/identity authority
* NOT a constitution. The law is CEP-002 Article 28. Every clause reference below is
a REFERENCE to that instrument; this file legislates nothing.
* NOT the finding register. Finding dispositions are a distinct subject owned by
The disposition set of 'dispositions' below IS CLOSED by CEP-002 Art 28.13. It is
extended only by amendment of CEP-002 under its Article 21. The lifecycle of
'lifecycle' below IS CLOSED by CEP-002 Art 28.8 on the same terms.

programme.name: Universal Constitutional Decision Assimilation
programme.$external_work_package_sources_comment: Located declarations whose own work packages are honoured as declared here. A decision whose work is already registered elsewhere references that package instead of duplicating it (Zero Duplication, CEP-002 8.3).

$outputs_comment: The determinations this programme regenerates, in the order the engine renders them.
File names and titles are DATA so that the engine holds no vocabulary of its own:
no stage name, no disposition name and no artifact name appears as a literal in the
engine source, which is what the no-enumeration self-check asserts.

outputs.title: Constitutional Decision Assimilation Dashboard
outputs.purpose: The single continuously-regenerated view of decision assimilation across the mandatory lifecycle.

outputs.title: 01 — Constitutional Decision Register
outputs.purpose: Every constitutionally agreed decision, the located register it was recorded in, the lifecycle stage it occupies, and its single disposition. A decision that appears nowhere but a conversation is not in this register and is not a decision of the Program.

outputs.title: 02 — Decision Lifecycle Determination
outputs.purpose: The mandatory decision lifecycle, its legal transitions, and the current occupancy of each stage. The set of stages is closed by the governing Article and is extended only by amending it.

outputs.title: 03 — Constitutional Disposition Register
outputs.purpose: The closed disposition set. Every agreed decision carries exactly one member, and each member carries its own mechanically checked evidence obligation. Nothing may remain ambiguous.

outputs.title: 04 — Implementation Evidence Gate Determination
outputs.purpose: No subsequent implementation programme, architectural work, or successor stage may be authorized while any previously ratified or recorded decision is undispositioned. The outcome below is computed from Repository Truth, never asserted.

outputs.title: 05 — Implementation Work Package Register
outputs.purpose: A work package is a registration of work, not a deferral of decision. Each names its owner, its constitutional route, and the acceptance condition by which it is discharged. This programme discharges nothing itself.

outputs.title: 06 — Decision Traceability Closure
outputs.purpose: The traceability spine of the decision population: decision → located register → index → disposition → located evidence. Every link below was resolved against the repository at generation time.

$lifecycle_comment: CEP-002 Art 28.8 — the mandatory decision lifecycle. Traversed in order (28.10); the
initial stage is the first entry and the terminal stage is the last (28.9). 'next'
declares the legal outgoing transitions. REPOSITORY-MAPPING carries the second legal
transition of 28.10 for dispositions that require no realization.
$dispositions_comment: CEP-002 Art 28.13 — the CLOSED disposition set. Every decision carries exactly one.
requires_fields          — fields the entry must carry, non-empty, for the disposition
to be valid. Absence makes the disposition VOID (28.13).
located_fields           — fields whose every value must RESOLVE to a repository path.
This is the mechanical expression of 28.5: Repository Truth
single_valued_fields     — fields that must carry exactly one value (28.13(b): two
canonical owners for one decision is a duplication finding).
decision_reference_fields— fields whose value must be a decision declared in this file
(28.13(e): no supersession against an unregistered successor).
work_package_fields      — fields whose value must be a work package declared below.
minimum_stage            — the earliest lifecycle stage at which the disposition may

dispositions.definition: The decision IS realized in the repository.
The substance of the decision IS already discharged by a located canonical owner and no further realization IS required.
The decision IS agreed but not yet realized, and IS carried by a located work package with an owner, a constitutional route and an acceptance condition.
The decision IS declined, on a constitutional basis cited to the governing clause.
The decision IS displaced by a later decision that IS itself registered and dispositioned.

decisions.title: Constitutional Reuse Gate as a NEW parallel gate
decisions.constitutional_basis: CEP-002 Art 8.3 (no governance power not established by the instrument; no parallel apparatus) · CEP-001 VII.2 (zero parallel architecture) · 03-ARCHITECTURAL-DECISION-ASSIMILATION-MATRIX.md §4 (Zero Parallel Architecture) · CMG-000001 CMG-INV-02 (a concern has exactly one owner)
decisions.justification: A second, independent reuse gate would duplicate the concern already owned by the located Context Assimilation Gate and would create two owners for one concern. The matrix records the duplication risk as HIGH if NEW and LOW via EXTEND, and expressly requires the reuse obligation to be formalized as a facet of the existing gate rather than as a parallel gate. The alternative is therefore declined on constitutional grounds, and the accepted form IS DEC-ADAM-10.
decisions.note: Recorded so that the rejected alternative cannot be silently revived. A rejection with a cited constitutional basis IS a disposition; an unrecorded rejection IS not.

decisions.title: Create a second, independent decision register to hold agreed decisions
decisions.constitutional_basis: CEP-002 Art 28.3 (a second decision register, store, pipeline, gate or authority IS PROHIBITED) · CEP-002 Art 8.3 · CEP-001 VII.2 (zero parallel architecture) · CMG-000001 CMG-INV-02 (one concern, one owner)
decisions.justification: The assimilation obligation could have been met by creating a new decision register that holds every agreed decision in one new place. That was declined: the corpus already contains located decision registers, and a new one would create a second owner for the decision concern and a second place a decision could be recorded and then diverge. The obligation is instead met by a disposition overlay that carries no decision of its own — every entry names the located register it was recorded in, and the engine requires that reference to resolve.
decisions.note: Recorded so that the rejected design cannot be silently revived, and so that this framework's own design alternatives are themselves dispositioned rather than left in conversation.
